title: Chaining: one project's data feeding another's
note: Provenance on every row works; milestones already read other projects' data (device tests); next: declared chains between projects. Settled 2026-11-11: parked: no project needs it yet; it returns with the first that does.

title: Changes in the observatory
note: Each project's changes linked to what they advanced and decided; work gone quiet becomes exact; a milestone shows the changes that moved it.

title: A changes table in the shared language
note: language.toml gains changes: id, date, kind (the conventional kinds: they set the version), summary, advances (backlog and milestone ids), decided, manual, breaking, released (filled by the release).

title: check reads a repository's essence
note: ocoeco check says how many of the four are told and what is still to tell - advice, never a failure.

title: ocoeco check validates every shared table
note: ocoeco check runs tad's check over each exported shared table with language.toml, so a hand-edited row outside the language is caught before the harvest - not only the row ocoeco note writes.

title: The core moved into ocoeco
note: The mark, discovery and the harvest live here as the ocoeco crate and command; the observatory gathers with it; the engine is only the face.

title: Every project gathers by itself
note: The principle lived: no project's data kept by hand.

title: The formats and protocols
note: tad (text as data) is the format ocoeco speaks: tables as JSON lines with a schema, canonical form, verification; the mark; to be specified here. Specified in SPEC.md (version 1).

title: Gathered data on its own branch; automation is not work
note: The gatherer committed to the default branch and then counted its own commits as activity, and a protected branch refused it. Now: the oco-data branch, path@branch in the mark, bots' and workflows' commits left out of activity; the marks of every repository to follow. Settled 2026-11-11: gatherers write to an oco-data branch in every marked project.

title: Gatherers: data made by work
note: Standard gatherers for activity, releases and CI: one reusable workflow, a five-line caller, running daily in all eleven marked repositories and written into each one's own oco/gathered/.

title: Test results as a standard gatherer
note: Device and project test runs gathered the same way everywhere (today: devlab writes them for surya).

title: Hand-work saturation: the table, the command, the views, land
note: Live 2026-11-11: the table, ocoeco hand (match, bump, or ask), the views (a page per project; hand-work worth a tool in the attention view, summed across projects), and land asking for --hand or --no-hand - a failure to record stops the landing.

title: Joining in one command
note: ocoeco init writes a repository's mark, the gatherer's caller and a place for its records (never overwriting); ocoeco check reads the repository as the harvest would. Fifteen repositories had been joined by hand-written scripts.

title: land and CI refuse a change with no record
note: land refuses; a reusable CI check from ocoeco fails a pull request without one; ocoeco hooks installs a local hook that points to ocoeco commit. Bots (feeds, update-pins, harvest) record through ocoeco commit too; dependency bumps get their record from the check's own exemption list.

title: Languages specified
note: SPEC section 9: the interface in Fluent catalogs, the data in each project's own translations table (by human or machine), applied only to that project's rows.

title: Lenses in the harvest
note: The lens kind; each lens.toml read into the lenses table; SPEC section 8.

title: ocoeco commit
note: Writes the change's record and renders the commit message from it (a conventional title, and trailers linking the record), then commits. Flags for agents and bots; later a picker. Every later commit on the branch reuses the record.

title: Recording as a tool: ocoeco note
note: One row added or updated, checked against the shared format; every other line untouched. Asked for by the author: no agent hand-writes a table again.

title: ocoeco release
note: Consumes unreleased records: the version from their kinds (highest wins), release notes grouped by milestone and backlog item, the version written, the records marked released, the tag set through land. First in shadow beside release-please on tad-engine, compared; then the switch, one project at a time; crates.io publishing for release-plz's two.

title: An interactive ocoeco in the terminal
note: First piece live 2026-11-11: ocoeco manual without an action - a list to narrow, choose, and record. Next: navigating and editing every table ocoeco holds. Settled 2026-11-11: first piece live (ocoeco manual opens a picker); navigating every table comes later.

title: One word for a concept's text: summary
note: The playbook and Rhizoid renamed their concepts' statement to summary (51 concepts; pages relabelled). All 22 projects now conform to language.toml.

title: The principle, written
note: Data is produced by projects as they are developed and as they function - never by hand. Specified in SPEC.md (version 1).

title: A project, whole: idea, path, workings, work
note: Specified (section 11), drawn by the engine, and read by ocoeco check. Projects are writing their ideas and workings. Settled 2026-11-11: SPEC section 11, the Essence view and ocoeco check's essence advice.

title: Propagation: the mark, discovery, the harvest
note: Working today in the observatory's engine; every row carries its project.

title: Shared tables read through the API
note: Current and authoritative; the raw file server cached for minutes and answered 501 to empty files on some runners.

title: Researched rows, research versions, staleness
note: Format: a row's research field (cited research id); research rows gain topic, supersedes and refresh_days. Engine: researched cells outlined with age and a link; a research page shows each topic's latest version with earlier ones in a disclosure; decisions citing an older version say a newer one exists; attention lists research past its horizon. First use: the Linux Phones landscape from other projects' claims, each with its source.

title: ocoeco as a rhizcut in every repository
note: Owned, patchable, sending fixes back; needs rhizoid v1.

title: tad's machinery in Rust
note: Verify, canonical form, schema and rendering - formats unchanged.

title: The vocabulary: a table, the shared words, the views
note: SPEC section 11 extended with the vocabulary table; ocoeco's own data defines the shared words first; ocoeco note and check learn its shape (a shared word redefined is flagged); the engine shows a vocabulary page and marks defined terms in a project's pages with their meaning beside them (no scripts). Done 2026-11-11: the table, ocoeco's 21 shared words, compiled into the tool; note and check know it. Next: the engine's views. Settled 2026-11-11: 27 shared words, each decided; vocabulary pages and decision badges.

title: Review every vocabulary, word by word
note: Done 2026-11-11 for ocoeco's shared words: each has its decision with the words rejected, citing the research on choosing words. Working became workings; load and saturated were added. Next: each project's own words, as they are written.

title: Waiting beside manual work
note: A waits table gathered from lab-agent; per project: time waited by what was waited on, beside manual effort, and flow efficiency (work over work plus waiting); in attention: the longest waits, as candidates for parallel work.
